correctness.rationale: For retained vertices in cyclic order, area=½Σ_j sin(K_j θ) and the missing area score f_n(k)=½(k sin θ−sin kθ), valid including one/two survivors; the zero-survivor event is handled separately and decays as q^n. A chord of index length k<n is a boundary edge exactly when both endpoints survive and k−1 interior vertices are deleted, probability p²q^(k−1). This gives the exact finite geometric series for EA_n. Taylor f_n(k)=θ³(k³−k)/12+O(θ^5(k^5+k)) with geometric gap tails makes the L² remainder O(n⁻⁴), negligible at n⁻⁵ᐟ². For geometric iid K, E K=1/p, g(K)=K³−K, a=E g(K)/E K=6q/p²; standard centered renewal-reward stopped-sum CLT and uniformly bounded wrap correction yield Var(S_n)/n→p E(g(K)−aK)^2=36q(1+q)(1+5q+q²)/p^5. Multiplying by (2π)^6/144 produces stated V_p; Slutsky gives the Gaussian law. Independent direct enumeration of retained subsets for n=4,5,6,7,9 and p=1/3,1/2 (10 configurations of parameter pairs) exactly corroborated finite mean; independent geometric-moment summations for p=.25,.4,.5,.75 agreed with V_p. Fixed p is essential, finite tests only corroborate analytical CLT.
residual_risks: The proof invokes standard renewal-reward CLT and a bounded L² boundary correction; tails are geometric at fixed p and make this justified, but no quantitative normal approximation or p→0 bound is shown.
Full high-n Monte Carlo portion of source checker was inspected but not executed in this independent run.

originality.rationale: Pardon proves CLTs for Poisson/interior i.i.d. random planar points in expanding convex settings, not Bernoulli occupancy of deterministic equally spaced boundary points. Koroleva–Nikitin studies random fixed-order polygons with continuous sampled locations on a circle; different counting/scaling. Pérez-Lantero studies the distribution/algorithmic complexity for finite sets of independent stochastic points, but its general algorithms do not provide this closed regular-vertex finite mean, sharp n^5 variance constant, or renewal CLT. Resultary semantic search returned no matching Bernoulli cyclic-gap theorem. The special model and explicit asymptotics are independently meaningful.
residual_risks: An unindexed renewal-reward treatment of Bernoulli-thinned convex polygons may reproduce the same asymptotic coefficients.
General stochastic finite-point distribution work may contain specialized regular-grid examples not indexed by present search terminology.

value.rationale: The theorem exactly identifies the n^(-5/2) Gaussian fluctuation scale, a closed variance coefficient and the full finite-n mean for an infinite, natural random-geometry model. These are useful as baseline asymptotic estimates for random vertex deletion, and neither standard renewal CLT alone nor finite computation supplies the geometric constant without the nontrivial cyclic-gap reduction.
residual_risks: Only fixed p∈(0,1); no sparse occupancy p=p_n asymptotic, no full finite-n area law.

final_claim: Fixed p∈(0,1), independently Bernoulli-retained vertices of a regular n-gon on the unit circle have the exact stated mean area, mean deficit 4π³q/(p²n²)−4π⁵q(1+q)²/(p⁴n⁴)+O(n⁻⁶), and n^(5/2)(A_n−EA_n) converges to N(0,V_p) with n^5 Var(A_n)→V_p=16π⁶q(1+q)(1+5q+q²)/p^5.
limitations: Sampling fixed n regular polygon vertices with fixed p, not continuous or interior random points or p_n→0/1.
Finite numerical corroboration not used to assert the CLT; renewal theorem proof is unrestricted at fixed p.
